newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A blueprint to develop the impoverished Northeast with a combination of modern technology and local skills has been approved by the cabinet. The blueprint, proposed by the National Economic and Social Development Board, focuses on boosting farm productivity, promoting the private sector role in development and promoting related and support industries. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Hazardous chemicals have been found poorly stored in a depot in the heart of Bangkok's Klong Toey port, the scene of a fatal toxic blast five years ago. The organic chemicals were found in substandard conditions in the private depot during an inspection by Kraisak Choonhavan, an adviser to the city governor, and Port Authority of Thailand officials. (BANGKOK POST)

- Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol has won the Cabinet's approval for his surprise reshuffle of three of the most senior Education Ministry officials one week after his controversial removal of a top executive of the Asian Games committee. (THE NATION)

- Globex Corp has rejected allegations that it was planning a third attempt at a hostile takeover of Phoenix Pulp and Paper Plc, saying it merely wants to see more transparent management. Globex director says he will raise questions tomorrow at the company's annual general meeting. (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan says he will solve the problems of finance and securities firms by means of market mechanism. Amnuay has not elaborated on the details but says he has ordered officials to study ways to mobilize funds for the industry. (BUSINESS DAY)
